searchText: If someone wants to join `merge-devnet-4`, configs and enr/enode have been published here: https://github.com/eth-clients/merge-testnets/tree/main/merge-devnet-4 Please do note that this is just a dress rehersal testnet, it is not meant as a replacement for Kintsugi. The aim of the testnet is to help us test a new spec version in a semi-public manner. Is there going to be a block explorer and fork/consensus monitor? Yup, probably a bit delayed but I will share the link. Gonna DM you the nimbus keys now got them, thanks Awesome <@!199561711278227457> ! hey <@!360491619402776577> is there a branch with which I can play with kilnV2 (config exchange + jwt auth)? Not yet, can build something for you if you have something, why not https://github.com/MariusVanDerWijden/go-ethereum/tree/merge-kiln-jwt Here you go one other question about command line. When i run a single local node, to start mining o run miner.start() in console (i'm using the same genesis.json of testnet-4). But it starts mining very fast and maxing out the cpu. using this command line ``` $GETH --networkid=1337752 --http --ws --http.api "admin,engine,net,eth" --http.port 8488 --datadir "${DATADIR}" --allow-insecure-unlock --unlock "0xa94f5374fce5edbc8e2a8697c15331677e6ebf0b" --password "" --bootnodes "" --mine --port 30323 console ``` should i do something different? You can use miner.start(1) to only start a single thread great thanks or --miner.threads 1 on startup or maybe switching to this https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ajsutton/merge-scripts/main/geku/execution-genesis.json ? You could do that too Will produce a block once every 5 seconds until ttd of 200 is reached yeah, more convenient. thnx We had multiple competing miners pre TTD and the eth1 chain had forked off. Some nodes observed a different terminal block than the others. However, the nodes did later on agree on just one terminal block and I guess re-orged to the correct chain as expected. So yaaay resilience 😄 The chain is continuing and finalizing as expected. Our beaconexplorer however relies on a lighthouse node, so we are unable to set one up at this time. The remaining tooling can be found here: https://devnet4.themerge.dev/ are these real, or? it's a bit odd that all of Nimbus, Prysm, and Teku have nodes doing this, while others nodes running are apparently mostly fine Noo, i think the monitor is off i'm ssh'ed into the node and they're all on the same head (prysm isn't, but its being looked into) Nice! How long did it take nodes to re-org to the correct chain, and how "deep" was the re-org? First terminal block was detected at 17:02 and the next one at 17:03, so not too long apart. The other forks were too far behind, so i think the nodes skipped forward to the one ahead. Got it, thanks!

excerpts.author: parithosh
excerpts.content: If someone wants to join `merge-devnet-4`, configs and enr/enode have been published here: https://github.com/eth-clients/merge-testnets/tree/main/merge-devnet-4

excerpts.author: parithosh
excerpts.content: Please do note that this is just a dress rehersal testnet, it is not meant as a replacement for Kintsugi. The aim of the testnet is to help us test a new spec version in a semi-public manner.

one other question about command line. When i run a single local node, to start mining o run miner.start() in console (i'm using the same genesis.json of testnet-4). But  it starts mining very fast and maxing out the cpu. using this command line
```
$GETH --networkid=1337752 --http --ws --http.api "admin,engine,net,eth" --http.port 8488 --datadir "${DATADIR}" --allow-insecure-unlock --unlock "0xa94f5374fce5edbc8e2a8697c15331677e6ebf0b" --password "" --bootnodes "" --mine --port 30323 console
```

excerpts.author: tbenr
excerpts.content: should i do something different?

excerpts.author: parithosh
excerpts.content:
We had multiple competing miners pre TTD and the eth1 chain had forked off. Some nodes observed a different terminal block than the others. However, the nodes did later on agree on just one terminal block and I guess re-orged to the correct chain as expected. So yaaay resilience 😄

The chain is continuing  and finalizing as expected. Our beaconexplorer however relies on a lighthouse node, so we are unable to set one up at this time. The remaining tooling can be found here: https://devnet4.themerge.dev/
